title: SLC-40 Final Environmental Assessment and Decision — Phase 65 Florida Space Coast authority and mission delivery review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Florida Space Coast authority and mission delivery reporting pack. The FAA's final environmental record analyzes expanded Falcon 9 operations and a booster landing zone at Cape Canaveral's SLC-40, including an envelope of up to 120 annual launches and 34 booster landings.
key_findings: The environmental review reaches a final decision for a defined expansion proposal.
The analyzed activity levels are a review envelope rather than achieved launch or landing throughput.
License modifications, construction, inspection, mitigation, mission execution, and safety outcomes remain separate.
why_it_matters: Which records connect licences, operators, infrastructure capital, construction, accepted facilities, mission use, safety, and repeat operations? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. The record provides a named Space Coast capacity-expansion trail while preventing environmental clearance from becoming an operating claim.
ftfn_relevance: Adds a project-level expansion decision to the Florida shelf.
Connects environmental review to licensing, build, mitigation, and utilization.
Supplies a bounded cadence envelope for later comparison with realized operations.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
The analyzed launch and landing counts are not forecasts or achieved volumes.
The decision is not every required license modification or construction approval.
It does not prove mitigation performance, safety, schedule, acceptance, or utilization.
